hypotheses.claim: For cvrp_ruin_recreate/v1 at a 500 ms budget, a ruin scoring hook that linearly blends node worst-cost removal saving (primary) with route slack/capacity-utilization and a stagnation_ratio-scaled deterministic jitter will lower total tour length versus a pure worst-cost-removal control (L3-ctrl), i.e. the LNS escapes local optima after stagnation without hurting the early anytime curve, because the jitter amplitude only grows once `stagnation_ratio` rises while `iter_frac` is still small enough to allow many further iterations.

next_search_advice.direction: Evolve the `score_ruin_nodes` hook toward a stagnation-adaptive, capacity-aware ruin priority: base term = normalized worst-cost removal saving (removal_savings / route_dists contribution of the node's route), modulated by route slack utilization (demand vs capacity) and a deterministic pseudo-random jitter whose amplitude scales with `stagnation_ratio` and `iter_frac`, so the LNS alternates between greedy worst-node destruction early and diversified related-destroy later; keep the ruin-size schedule tied to iter_frac so late iterations widen the removed set.
